profile_text.body:
Writesonic is a San Francisco, California company that describes itself as an AI search growth engine, positioning its platform around what it calls GEO (generative engine optimization), AEO (answer engine optimization), and AI visibility. The company's site states the platform tracks visibility across 10 AI platforms and more than 50 markets, drawing on a dataset it describes as covering 2 billion or more real AI conversations updated weekly. It names Amazon, Unilever, Acer, and NP Digital as customers.

The platform's core workflow, which Writesonic calls the AI Search Loop, is presented as a cycle of identifying where a brand lacks visibility in AI-generated results, running fixes through content rewrites, citation building, and technical audits, and then measuring results at Day 14 and Day 28 intervals. Specific features include an AI agent that rewrites pages to add FAQ blocks, comparison tables, and passages intended to earn citations from AI engines, tools to audit robots.txt, schema, and crawler errors from bots such as GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot, and outreach drafting aimed at the third-party sites the company says account for 85 percent of AI citations. The platform also offers product-level tracking aimed at placements in ChatGPT Shopping and similar recommendation surfaces, along with white-label and multi-client tooling for agencies.

The site's held facts record Writesonic as headquartered in San Francisco with a tracked product, WriteSonic, categorized under writing and editing with a note of marketing copy. The site also carries 175 California law exposure entries associated with the company, though no specific litigation cases are on record.
